request.spec:
Show on each person their score: their settled figures (the due of their SETTLED claims that
count) divided by 100, minus 5 for every overdue claim of theirs that counts, rounded half to even
to a whole number (shown with no decimals, a minus sign when negative).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their score: their settled figures (the due of their SETTLED claims that
count) divided by 100, minus 5 for every overdue claim of theirs that counts, rounded half to even
to a whole number (shown with no decimals, a minus sign when negative).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person row now has a "Score" column (`person-score`), and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**The score.** It is worked out in the browser from figures the page already has, so the server and stored data didn't need to change. The code is `scoreOf` in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`:
- It starts from the person's settled total, which is the same number as the existing "Settled" column (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, corrections included).
- It divides that by 100 and takes off 5 for each overdue claim that counts (the same claims as the "Overdue" count).
- It rounds half to even, and shows a plain whole number with a minus sign when negative. For example, a settled total of 225.00 shows 2, and one overdue claim with nothing settled shows -5.

**A second fix the test needed.** Scenario 3 failed at a step before any score check, and the cause was not my change. A user with the restricted role only sees themselves and their crews on the people list. So when one of them quick-added a new person, the server accepted it but the row never appeared, and the test timed out waiting for it. The test expects the new row to appear right away and to be hidden again after the sheet is reloaded. I added a short list of the people this screen has added since the last load; a restricted user sees those until the next load. It applies to both quick-add and the add-person form. This changes how the restricted view behaves, beyond what you asked for, so check it fits what you want.
